handbookNote: Oklahoma Notary Public Law, Title 49 O.S. -- APPLICATION-ONLY state: no state-administered exam and no mandatory training course exist (confirmed via the Oklahoma Secretary of State's own commissioning process and corroborated by the National Notary Association). This is therefore self-study/reference practice content grounded in real statute text, NOT exam prep -- no pass/fail claim, no implied official passing score. Statute is unusually fragmented across THREE separate sub-acts within Title 49: (1) the base Notary Public Act, 49 O.S. SS 1-12 (several sections repealed, ~11-12 operative covering appointment, application, oath/bond/seal, authority, and revocation); (2) the older, pre-RULONA Uniform Law on Notarial Acts, 49 O.S. SS 111-121 (11 sections, enacted 1985, covering acknowledgments/verifications/certificates and interstate/foreign recognition -- distinct from the modern Revised Uniform Law on Notarial Acts other states use); and (3) the comparatively modern and detailed Remote Online Notary Act, 49 O.S. SS 201-214 (14 sections, effective 2020, covering RON registration, procedures, journal/recording retention, and fees). Roughly 33-37 operative sections total. Unusual/high-friction requirements found during scoping: Oklahoma notaries must pass a national criminal history background check via the OSBI AND post a $10,000 surety bond -- one of the highest notary bond amounts of any state scoped in this project -- with total upfront cost (bond + $50 filing fee + up to $50 background-check fee) landing around $220, well above the typical application-only state. Content depth rationale: given the three-sub-act breadth, target was ~150 grounded MCQs; deliberate care was taken to write distinct, non-redundant questions rather than restating the same rule once per sub-act where the base Act and Uniform Law sections cover overlapping ground (e.g. notarial authority, identity verification). Pricing: $0.75 (75 cents) -- OK was originally on this project's 'skip entirely' list for application-only states (no exam/quiz/assessment of any kind, so no 'pass' framing fits) per the 2026-08-15 decision documented in this project's memory; this track was built as an explicit one-off exception at a new, lower price point (below the $0.99 AL/FL/GA/TX education-only tier and far below the $9.99 exam-state tier) specifically because it is pure state-law reference content with no assessment attached, not because the underlying law is thin -- the three-sub-act structure and $10,000 bond actually make Oklahoma's notary law deeper than most application-only states.
